---
# A real title is needed: with an empty one, Quarto promotes the page's first
# heading ("Research Interests") into the title block, which pushed it above the
# hero and orphaned its list. The title block is hidden below — the hero is the
# page's visible heading.
title: "Harjoat S. Bhamra"
pagetitle: "Harjoat S. Bhamra"
toc: false
---

```{python}
#| output: asis
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd()))
from _helpers import load

p = load("profile")
bio = " ".join(w for w in p["bio_paragraph"].split() if w)
hero_links = "".join(f'<a href="{p["links"][k]}">{label}</a>' for k, label in [
    ("google_scholar", "Google Scholar"),
    ("ssrn", "SSRN"),
    ("repec", "RePEc"),
    ("orcid", "ORCID"),
    ("cepr", "CEPR"),
    ("niesr", "NIESR"),
    ("imperial_faculty", "Imperial"),
])
hero_html = (
    # Hide Quarto's own title block on this page only; the hero below is the h1.
    '<style>#title-block-header { display: none; }</style>'
    f'<div class="hero">'
    f'<div class="hero-text">'
    f'<h1>{p["name"]["display"]}</h1>'
    f'<p class="subtitle">{p["title"]}<br>{p["affiliation"]["short"]}</p>'
    f'<p>{bio}</p>'
    f'<div class="profile-links">'
    f'<a href="mailto:{p["contact"]["email"]}">{p["contact"]["email"]}</a>'
    f'{hero_links}'
    f'</div>'
    f'</div>'
    f'<div class="hero-image"><img src="profile.jpg" alt="Harjoat S. Bhamra"></div>'
    f'</div>'
)
print("::: {=html}")
print(hero_html)
print(":::")
```

## Selected Recent Work

```{python}
#| output: asis
from _helpers import load, render_paper
pubs = load("publications")
# Show the three most recent published papers, then the top three working papers
shown = []
shown += pubs.get("published", [])[:3]
shown += [p for p in pubs.get("working", [])[:3] if not p.get("skip_website")]
for p in shown:
    print(render_paper(p))
```
